1. [✓] Query UniProt for canonical human ANGPTL7 (O43827) and HNRNPC (P07910)
2. [✓] Recompute masses from full primary sequences
3. [✓] Identified and diagnosed the P07910 anomaly (index fields say 382 aa / 42,088 Da; deposited sequence is 306 aa / 33,670 Da)
4. [✓] Cross-validated against curated NCBI RefSeq: ANGPTL7 NP_066969.1 = 346 aa; HNRNPC NP_112604.2 (C1) = 306 aa, NP_004491.2 (C2) = 293 aa
5. [✓] Compared masses and identified the heavier gene symbol

**Results**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANGPTL7 (angiopoietin-related protein 7) | O43827 | 346 aa | **40.02 kDa** (40,018 Da) |
| HNRNPC (hnRNP C1/C2) | P07910 | 306 aa | **33.67 kDa** (33,670 Da) |

ANGPTL7 is heavier by ~6.35 kDa. Both values were independently confirmed by recomputing the molecular weight from the primary sequence (Biopython `molecular_weight`) and by curated RefSeq proteins (NP_066969.1 = 346 aa; NP_112604.2 = 306 aa; the C2 isoform NP_004491.2 is 293 aa = 32.34 kDa, still lighter than ANGPTL7).

**Concerns:** The UniProt entry P07910 is internally inconsistent — its ID/SQ header lines and the `length`/`molWeight` fields report **382 AA / 42,088 Da**, but the actual deposited sequence (JSON `sequence.value`, FASTA, and flat-file) is only **306 aa / 33,670 Da**, reproducible across all endpoints. RefSeq supports the 306-aa C1 isoform, so I used 33.67 kDa. Note this matters for the answer: if the anomalous 42,088 Da figure were taken at face value, HNRNPC would appear heavier than ANGPTL7 (40.02 kDa). I judged the 306-aa/33.67 kDa value to be correct.
